content:
maya: quick sanity run for encore-v2 int8 on wiki-holdout — recall@1 roughly OK but recall@10 drops ~6% vs fp16. odd.
samir: can you paste the exact eval command? :thinking_face:
maya: `python eval.py --model encore-v2 --quant int8 --dataset wiki-holdout --k 1,10,100 --batch 256`
linh: did you use per-channel quant or per-tensor symmetric?
maya: per-channel, using our onnx-int8 pipeline; calib set N=2000
arnold: what were the ANN index params? ef/search and PQ?
maya: ef=200, M=32, PQ=16 (built with hnsw + pq to match prod)
samir: any change in embedding norms or cosine distribution?
maya: good call — mean norm decreased from 1.02 -> 0.88 after quant, cosine mean shift ~0.04, std increased slightly
tracy: that could explain k>1 drop. quant can shrink activations. try scale clipping or bias correction during quantization
maya: starting a run with per-channel scale clamping (clip 0.05) and asymmetric zero-point compensation
linh: also run brute-force exact NN (no PQ) on a smaller shard to rule out index artifacts
maya: queued brute-force (10k queries, exact search), ETA ~2h
samir: if brute-force recall aligns with fp16, then PQ/HNSW params are likely at fault. if brute-force also drops, quant pipeline is culprit.
deploy-bot: job started: eval/2180539000-encore-int8-scale-clamp (job id job-encore-9001)
arnold: also check per-dimension scale histograms — some dims blow up after quant, others collapse. per-channel clipping helps often
maya: copying logs here after initial clamp run: 
```
SUMMARY: recall@1: 0.872 (fp16 0.875)
         recall@10: 0.702 (fp16 0.764)  <-- large gap
EMBED_NORM_MEAN: 0.88 -> 1.02 (delta -0.14)
COSINE_MEAN_SHIFT: 0.039
```
linh: yikes recall@10 gap is real. what's dist metric? cosine?
maya: cosine. ran also with inner-product; similar pattern.
tracy: try re-normalizing embeddings post-quant as a quick mitigation and re-run recall@k. if that recovers most, we can push temp fix while root-cause triaged
maya: launching renorm pass now, small shard first
samir: also double-check calibration dataset composition — if calib set skewed short queries it can bias scales
maya: calib is 2k random wiki passages; will try stratified calib with long+short mix
arnold: thumbs if you want me to run a wider sweep of clipping thresholds (0.01/0.05/0.1)
maya: please do 0.01 and 0.1 runs, thanks
samir: ping me if brute-force matches fp16, I'll dig into PQ rebuild params (norm-preserving PQ configs exist)
maya: will update with brute-force numbers and clamp sweep results. thanks all :pray:
